A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Sigmoid Head study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across additions and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original quality-estimation experiments on translation, paraphrasing and question answering, including negative-sampling ablations. Appendix E additionally reports word-level results.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F retain the original quantitative experiments. Appendix G adds scored translation examples and qualitative analysis.

M1.justification: Both versions use a frozen language model, an additional sigmoid head, ten sampled negatives and dominant-token exclusion. The added inference and score-aggregation explanations provide documentation without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Appendix G adds WMT23 German-to-English translation coverage through six illustrative cases. The existing training and quantitative evaluation datasets, including the appendix's HJQE evaluation, are retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain Softmax Head, BoostedProb, COMET Kiwi, Monte Carlo sequence-entropy variants, LLM Self Judge and supervised OpenKiwi. The new qualitative comparison uses the existing Softmax comparator; the added NCE background introduces no evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix G introduces manual inspection of selected translations, comparing human scores, Tower Instruct v2 quality scores and probabilities of alternative words. Existing quantitative protocols remain unchanged. Multiplication of token scores is newly disclosed, without a reported revision to the earlier evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: New Appendix D analyzes parameter overhead, while Appendix G examines cases where adequate translations receive low softmax scores. These are focused supplementary analyses; the negative-sampling ablations in Figure 2 and Table 6 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate reporting practice. There are no additions or revisions to seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2–6 and the word-level results in v1 Table 8/v2 Table 9 retain their values. v2 adds parameter-overhead results and six qualitative result rows. For example, Table 10's first case reports human, Sigmoid and Softmax scores of 0.98, 0.99 and 0.02.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the definition of N_i: v1 equates it with the entire eligible vocabulary, while v2 identifies it as negatives sampled from that pool. This aligns the BCE loss sum with the stated ten-negative procedure. Appendix A's derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: ambiguity-aware quality estimation without human quality labels, computational efficiency, stronger quality signals and robustness under domain shift. The added material does not redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: The Limitations section and new Appendix D acknowledge parameter and memory overhead and explain its dependence on model and vocabulary size. This adds a substantive qualification, particularly for DeltaLM and OLMo 1B, while retaining the previous interpretations and limitations.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents multiplication of token scores, clarifies inference, and reports parameter counts with the added head. It also updates the stated code location from sigmoid-confidence to sigmoid-head-qe. Existing hardware and training disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and Section 6's positioning against NCE, SCONES and probability-adjustment methods remain unchanged. New Section 2.3 expands background on already cited NCE; the Tulu and OLMo reference edits update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: v2 adds an NCE background subsection, localized method explanations and two appendix sections, with corresponding cross-reference and heading edits. Contact information and acknowledgements also change. The main narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the parameter-count table and a full-width qualitative-example table. Existing appendix tables are renumbered and displays reflow around added text. Figures 1–2 retain their content, and the overall two-column presentation remains.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility by specifying score aggregation, corrects the sampled-negative loss definition, and quantifies previously undocumented parameter overhead, including 30.8% for DeltaLM and 20.6% for OLMo. The selected translation cases add useful illustration. These targeted gains improve clarity and transparency while leaving the main performance evidence and claims substantially unchanged.
